---
name: proofpress
description: Preserve decision history for Markdown knowledge artifacts with Proofpress. Use when creating or accepting a meaningful revision to an ADR, design doc, PRD, README, strategy note, or portable .md artifact in a repository containing proofpress.py; never use for source-code files.
---

Record accepted Markdown artifact versions with structured testimony and
verification. Do not snapshot every conversational turn.
1. Read `python3 proofpress.py policy <file>`. If the user asks for portability,

run `policy <file> portable` once; it remains sticky. If Git history exists
   without a ledger, run `ingest <file>`.
2. Preserve surviving `[//]: # (ob:xxxxxxxx)` anchors while editing. Run
3. Write claims JSON with one honest entry per touched or removed block; do not
4. Snapshot the accepted version with `--why`, claims, and explicit actors:

```sh
   python3 proofpress.py snapshot <file> --kind agent --author claude \
     --produced-by claude --recorded-by claude \
     --attribution-basis "active authoring session" --note "<changelog>" \
     --claims <claims.json> --why "<actual reason>" \
     --rejected "<consequential dead branch — reason>"
   ```

Omit `--rejected` unless the dead branch matters to future collaborators.
   Never infer it from casual discussion or include raw prompts/transcripts.
5. Run `verify <file>` and report its output verbatim. Never re-snapshot merely

For incoming portable files, run `inspect` and then `import`. Fallback `capture`
records only `recorded_by`; it cannot know authorship or reasoning. Never
snapshot source-code files.
